title: Chaman Lal Setia Exports Ltd-$ - 530307 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q2 FY27 PBT of about INR 75 crore, management calls it the best quarter ever, helped by high paddy-rice prices and a weaker rupee.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the best quarter in company history, with PBT of around INR 75 crore. Gains were attributed to inventory bought at lower prices in 2025 and a rupee near INR 94-96 per USD. Volumes fell year-on-year, which management linked to Middle East war-related shipping delays and high ocean freight. Management said it does not expect the same margins to persist and that it has slowed procurement at current paddy prices.

financial_highlights.change: described as the best quarter ever; no YoY figure stated

financial_highlights.metric: Basmati realisation (per company PPT, as cited by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: analyst cited Q-on-Q basis; not confirmed by management
management says this is the normal margin, not windfall

segments.name: Basmati export business
segments.commentary: Main business; management targets 6.5 million tonnes of exports this year, and says it will meet or exceed that. Export is said to be growing gradually, with Nesto in Dubai (151 outlets) as a large buyer. Sales are to about 95-96 countries.

segments.name: Domestic India marketing
segments.commentary: Management said it has been trying to build an India marketing business for 5-6 months, but export is more lucrative, so the effort has been deprioritised for now.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the transit delays from the war to normalise in about a fortnight, if the conflict does not escalate further.
Management does not expect the current margins to be sustained: it said it is unlikely to earn the same ratios going forward and that prices may fall.
Management aims to achieve the 6.5 million tonne export target this year, and said it might increase it.
Management said it is buying paddy more slowly than last year and buying only where it can earn a margin.
Management said a weaker rupee (INR 96-98 per USD forecasts it cited) would add to profits, but it is not a forecast it commits to.
capex_capacity: Capex is ongoing to replace old machinery with new plants and automation for grain movement and packing, to reduce labour dependence.
Management said existing capacity is already very large and that new plants are replacing old machinery rather than adding volume.
Cost-saving initiatives mentioned include water recycling and heat-loss reduction by a brother (Vijay Setia), and paying ocean freight in USD to save about INR 3 per USD-equivalent on invoices.
demand_pricing: Paddy and rice prices are high: 1509 Sella parboiled rose from INR 55-57/kg (Diwali last year) to about INR 84-85/kg now; 1718 and 1121 steam rose from INR 64-66/kg to above INR 100/kg; parboiled about INR 91-92/kg.

Iran-linked buying is a key driver of current high prices. Management said Iran buyers booked vessels for 5,000-10,000 tonnes per shipment. The company does not export to Iran (stopped about 25 years ago).
Ocean freight to Dubai rose from USD 200-250 per container to USD 5,500-6,000. The company sells FOB and ships CIF, passing freight costs to buyers.
Management said some buyers are deferring purchases because of high prices and freight, and may slow buying for 1-2 months before resuming.
Acreage for Basmati fell 1-4% (Haryana about 4%), but yields rose to 24-25 quintal per acre from 20 quintal, per management.
A Saudi customer ordered 500 tonnes last year and has placed 200 tonnes more; the customer says it can buy 250,000 tonnes. Price has not been agreed.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company have exposure to Iran, and how is shipping?
qa_highlights.answer: No exports to Iran for about 25 years, not even via Dubai. Management says large Iran exporters carry huge exposures and it asks for 100% advance payment if approached.

qa_highlights.question: Will realisations move to INR 110-112 per kg this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said anything is possible but would not confirm. It said prices depend on buyer timing and that the market can move quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Middle East war disrupt volumes this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buyers may defer buying when prices are high, and that some slowdown may spill into the last month or two of the quarter. It did not quantify the impact.

qa_highlights.question: How much have procurement costs risen, and what are the inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it built large stock in 2025 at low prices, which drove profitability. It said it cannot give the same margins going forward and gave a 1509 price rise of about INR 30-40/kg as the comparison.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company return the cash through a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would consider the suggestion but gave no commitment.

risks_watch: Margin normalisation: management said it does not expect Q2-level margins to be repeated as paddy and rice prices are high.
Middle East shipping: freight to the Gulf rose sharply and transit times lengthened; management expects normalisation in about a fortnight, which is uncertain.
Rupee: management's gains depend on a weaker rupee; a stronger rupee would reduce profits.
Iran-linked demand: a key driver of current prices, and it could end suddenly.
Volume decline: volumes fell YoY in Q2, and management did not quantify the shortfall or the spill-over into Q3.
Pending information: inventory tonnage at end-September was not answered on the call and was to be followed up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's results and the export outlook, but cautious on forward margins, which management said will not stay at current levels. Evasive on specifics: it did not give realisation, inventory, or cost figures, and deferred the buyback and India-business questions.
key_quotes: Normal profitability is coming, not the windfall gains at this moment.
We have slowed down our procurement, really speaking. We are buying if we can sell at a margin.
So, there is a possibility the prices may come down.

adds.what: Capex replacing old machinery with new plants and automation for grain movement and packing (no added volume stated)

growth.why: Management targets 6.5 million tonnes of exports this year and says it will meet it, but Q2 volumes fell YoY, management does not expect current margins to persist, and the capex is replacement of old machinery rather than added volume, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said Q2 FY27 PBT of about INR 75 crore came from 2025 low-cost inventory and it does not expect these margins to persist; it cites 8-10% as the normal margin and paddy/1509 prices up about INR 30-40/kg.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management said existing capacity is already very large and new plants replace old machinery rather than add volume; no new capacity timing was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 6.5 million tonnes of exports this year and says it will meet it, but Q2 volumes fell YoY, buyers may defer 1-2 months, and the shortfall was not quantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is replacement of old machinery and automation, with no utilisation figure or new capacity plan disclosed; no fresh capex announcement was flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to confirm realisations of INR 110-112/kg and said weaker-rupee gains are not a committed forecast; the tone points to caution on forward earnings.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects margins to fall and prices may decline, and Q2 benefited from low-cost 2025 inventory, so earnings are likely to normalise from the record quarter's PBT of about INR 75 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launch was discussed; the domestic India marketing push has been deprioritised.

rows.label: Saudi customer volume opportunity
rows.why: A Saudi customer ordered 500 tonnes last year, placed 200 tonnes more, and says it can buy 250,000 tonnes, but price is not agreed.

rows.label: Middle East shipping normalisation
rows.why: Management expects transit delays to normalise in about a fortnight if the conflict does not escalate, with Dubai freight up from USD 200-250 to USD 5,500-6,000 per container.

rows.label: Cost savings from freight and water recycling
rows.why: Management is paying ocean freight in USD to save about INR 3 per USD-equivalent on invoices, and is pursuing water recycling and heat-loss reduction.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record quarter and the 6.5 million tonne export target but cautious on forward margins, and evasive on realisations, inventory and the buyback; analysts pushed on realisations of INR 110-112/kg and volume impact.
